announcements.text: Lockheed Martin Corp., Fort Worth, Texas, is awarded an $871,243,964 modification (P00002) to a cost-plus-incentive-fee indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract (N0001926D0010). This modification increases the contract ceiling to provide additional capacity for support equipment under the F-35 Lightning II site activation and hardware non-recurring sustainment effort. The contract provides initial sustainment supplies and services in support of establishing and activating land-based and at-sea F-35 operational sites for the Air Force, Marine Corps, Navy, Cooperative Program Partners, and Foreign Military Sales customers. Work will be performed in El Segundo, California (90%) and Fort Worth, Texas (10%), and is expected to be completed in February 2031. No funds will be obligated at the time of award; funds will be obligated on individual orders as they are issued. This modification was not competitively procured. Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

Walsh Federal LLC, Chicago, Illinois, is awarded a $191,286,000 firm-fixed-price contract for construction services for Marine Corps barracks at Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune in North Carolina. Work is expected to be completed by August 2030. The maximum dollar value, including the base price and thirteen options, is $270,999,119. Fiscal 2026 Operations and Maintenance, Marine Corps, funds in the amount of $191,286,000 will be obligated at the time of the award and will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website, with four offers received. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Mid-Atlantic, Norfolk, Virginia, is the contracting activity (N40085-26-C-0023).

MEB General Contractors Inc., Chesapeake, Virginia, was awarded a $96,262,000 firm-fixed-price, award-fee-incentive with economic-price-adjustment contract for construction of P732 Electrical Distribution System Upgrades (Gosport Substation) at Norfolk Naval Shipyard. The maximum dollar value, including unexercised options and potential award fee, is $113,797,000. Work will be performed at Portsmouth, Virginia, and is expected to complete by September 2032. The contract will be incrementally funded with Military Construction, Navy funds. Fiscal 2026 Military Construction, Navy funds in the amount of $58,523,567 will be obligated at time of award. This contract was competitively procured via SAM.gov, with six offers received. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Atlantic, Norfolk, Virginia, is the contracting activity (N62470-26-C-0009).

Lockheed Martin Space, Titusville, Florida is being awarded a $76,562,774 Cost-Plus-Incentive-Fee modification (P00032) to previously award and announced contract (N0003024C0100) for TRIDENT II (D5) Life Extension 2 (D5LE2) SSP Alteration (SPALT) Advanced Design and Development Program efforts. Work will be performed in Denver, Colorado (51%); Elkton, Maryland (9%); Montville, New Jersey (7%); Greeneville, Tennessee (6%) Cape Canaveral (5%); Pittsfield, Massachusetts (4%); Sunnyvale, California (2%); Titusville, Florida (2%); Mason, Ohio (2%); Lancaster, Pennsylvania (2%); Kings Bay, Georgia (1%); Louisville, Kentucky (1%); and locations less than 1.0 percent each, 8% total. Work is expected to be completed Sept. 30, 2030. Fiscal 2026 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $76,562,774 will be obligated on this modification award and no funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract is being awarded to the Contractor on a sole source basis under 10 U.S. Code 2304(a)(1) and was previously synopsized on the Systems for Award Management (SAM) website, with one proposal received. Strategic Systems Programs, Washington, D.C, is the contracting activity.

Honeywell Aerospace Technologies, Minneapolis, Minnesota, is being awarded $53,866,460 for a firm-fixed-price contract for the procurement of up to 1125 components over five years representing three different parts used in ring laser gyros that are components of and support the WSN-7 inertial navigation system used on a variety of Navy submarines and surface ships. This is a five-year base contract with no option periods. All work will be performed in Minneapolis, Minnesota. No funds are being obligated at time of award. Subsequent delivery orders under the resultant five-year contract will be issued by September 2031 and funded with appropriate fiscal year working capital funds (Navy) and those funds will not expire. One source was solicited for this sole-source requirement pursuant to the authority set forth in 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1) and one offer was received. Naval Supply Systems Command Weapon Systems Support, Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity (N00104-26-D-AZ01).

Kato Engineering Inc., North Mankato, Minnesota, is awarded a $49,260,781 firm-fixed-price, cost-plus-fixed-fee, cost indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for programmatic, engineering, logistics, configuration management, diminishing manufacturing sources and material shortages, repairs and overhauls, technical support, logistics product updates, data calls and meeting support, and program planning support for the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System Energy Storage Subsystem in support of in-service Ford-class aircraft carriers. Work will be performed in North Mankato, Minnesota (80%); Portsmouth, Virginia (18%); and Lakehurst, New Jersey (2%), and is expected to be completed in September 2031. No funds will be obligated at the time of award; funds will be obligated on individual orders as they are issued. This contract was not competitively procured. Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity (N0001926D1010).

Woodward HRT Inc., Valencia, California, is being awarded $41,515,920 for a firm-fixed-price contract for the repair of 545 hydraulic power drive units supporting Navy/Marine/Air Force V-22 Osprey sustainment. This is a two-year requirements long-term contract with no option periods. All work will be performed in Santa Clarita, California. No funds are being obligated at time of award. Subsequent delivery orders under the resultant two-year contract will be issued by December 2028 with work being completed by September 2029. Subsequent delivery orders will be funded with appropriate fiscal year working capital funds (Navy) and those funds will not expire. One source was solicited for this sole-source requirement pursuant to the authority set forth in 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1) and one offer was received. Naval Supply Systems Command Weapon Systems Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity (N00383-26-D-0015).

SLSCO Ltd., Galveston, Texas, is awarded a $30,519,900 modification to a firm-fixed-price contract for construction of an aircraft parking apron and supporting facilities at Royal Australian Air Force Base, Darwin, Australia. The total cumulative face value of the contract is $490,841,516. The contract modification provides for an increase in estimated quantity for asbestos containing material encountered onsite. Work will be performed in Darwin, Australia, and is expected to complete by May 2028. Fiscal 2025 and 2026 military construction (Navy) funds in the amount of $10,028,333 and $20,491,567 are obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Pacific, Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii, is the contracting activity (N62742-25-C-1308).

Huntington Ingalls Inc. Newport News Shipbuilding, Virginia, is awarded a $28,520,626 cost-plus-fixed fee modification to previously awarded Contract (N00024-24-C-2106) for additional advance planning effort for the accomplishment of the USS Harry S. Truman (CVN 75) Refueling Complex Overhaul. Work will be performed in Newport News, Virginia. Fiscal 2026 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $28,520,626 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

Bell Boeing Joint Project Office, Amarillo, Texas, is awarded a $19,785,639 cost-plus-fixed-fee order (N0001926F0331) under a previously awarded basic ordering agreement (N0001922G0002). This order provides engineering, management, technical, and acquisition support to sustain the V-22 Tactical Software Suite in support of maintaining the operational readiness of the V-22 fleet for the Air Force, Marine Corps, and Navy. Work will be performed in Ridley Park, Pennsylvania (59%); Fort Worth, Texas (30%); Amarillo, Texas (10%); Albuquerque, New Mexico (1%) and is expected to be completed in April 2030. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $8,028,373; fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance (Air Force) funds in the amount of $6,231,511; fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Air Force) funds in the amount of $1,824,567; fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $2,874,307; fiscal 2026 aircraft procurement (Air Force) funds in the amount of $404,306; fiscal 2026 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $308,333; and fiscal 2026 procurement (Defense-Wide) funds in the amount of $114,242 will be obligated at the time of award. This contract was not competed. Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

Leidos Inc., Reston, Virgina, has been awarded a not-to-exceed $85,000,000 ceiling indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity contract for Digital System-Level Mission-Driven Integrated Design Methods for Aerospace Systems. This contract provides research to enable a vehicle system design product and thermal management system design methodologies. Work will be performed at Dayton, Ohio, and is expected to be completed by Sept. 18, 2036. This contract was a competitive acquisition and eight offers were received. No funds are obligated on the basic indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity contract, however, in conjunction with the basic contract, the first Task Order (FA2391-26-F-B022) is incrementally funded with Fiscal 2026 research and development funds in the amount of $75,000. The Air Force Research Laboratory, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity (FA2391-26-D-B015).

The Boeing Company, Long Beach, California, was awarded a $34,286,429 order for production of Replacement Heads Up Display (RHUD), Phase C. This order provides for delivery of RHUD mod kits and spares part kits. Work will be performed at Long Beach, California, Mesa, Arizona, and is expected to be completed by July 2, 2029. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 24 procurement funds in amount of $12,635,625 and fiscal 25 procurement funds in amount of $21,650,804 are being obligated at time of award. The C-17 Contracting Branch, Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, is the contracting activity (FA8526-26-F-B016).

Raytheon Co., managed by Collins Aerospace Mission Secured Solutions, McKinney, Texas, has been awarded a $9,578,404 modification (P00007) to a previously awarded contract (FA2385-24-C-B037) for the Defense Experimentation Using Commercial Space Internet program. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $135,325,185 from $125,746,781. Work will be performed at McKinney, Texas and is expected to be completed by Aug. 29, 2028. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $9,578,404 are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Research Laboratory, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity.

BP Products North America Inc., Chicago, Illinois (SPE602-26-D-0493, $601,895,915); Valero Marketing and Supply Co., San Antonio, Texas (SPE602-26-D-0488, $432,153,244); Chevron U.S.A. Inc., San Ramon, California (SPE602-26-D-0484, $418,046,114); Marathon Petroleum Co. LP, Findlay, Ohio (SPE602-26-D-0487, $307,603,912); Petro Star Inc.,* Anchorage, Alaska (SPE602-26-D-0485, $234,142,421); Par Hawaii Refining LLC, Houston, Texas (SPE602-26-D-0495, $135,812,649); Avfuel Corp., Ann Arbor, Michigan (SPE602-26-D-0486, $68,853,541); U.S. Oil and Refining Co., Tacoma, Washington (SPE602-26-D-0492, $63,729,764); Lazarus Energy Holdings LLC,* Houston, Texas (SPE602-26-D-0490, $28,666,455) and Hermes Consolidated LLC, doing business as Wyoming Refining Co., Houston, Texas (SPE602-26-D-0491, $25,798,171) have each been awarded a fixed-price with economic-price-adjustment, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract under solicitation (SPE602-26-R-0702) for various types of fuel. This was a competitive acquisition with twenty-seven responses received. These are one-year contracts with a thirty-day carryover. Locations of performance are Alaska, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Montana, New Mexico, Texas, Utah, Washington and Wyoming, with an Oct. 30, 2027, performance completion date. Using customer is Defense Logistics Agency. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2027 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Energy, Fort Belvoir, Virginia.

US Foods Salem, Salem, Missouri, has been awarded a maximum $67,625,878 modification (P00005) to a five-year contract (SPE300-21-D-3317) with a 364-day carryover for full-line food and beverage items. This is a firm-fixed-price with economic-price-adjustment, indefinite-delivery/indefinite quantity contract. The ordering period end date is Sept. 18, 2027. Using military services are Air Force and Army. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2027 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

L3Harris Cincinnati Electronics Corp., Mason, Ohio, has been awarded a maximum $25,241,883 firm‐fixed‐price, indefinite-delivery requirements contract for Avenger Forward-Looking Infrareds. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (c)(2), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302‐1. This is a five-year contract with no option periods. The performance completion date is Sept. 17, 2031. Using military service is Army. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2031 Army working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapon Support, Redstone Arsenal, Alabama (SPRRA2-26-D-0013).

CORRECTION: The contract announced on Sept. 15, 2026, for American Material Handling Inc.,* Watkinsville, Georgia (SPE8EC-26-D-0025) for $86,000,000 was announced with an incorrect award date. The correct award date is Sept. 16, 2026. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

HSGS-Ameresco LLC,* Summerville, South Carolina, was awarded a $51,572,833 firm-fixed-price contract for design-bid-build construction of a power generation and microgrid project at Anniston Army Depot. Bids were solicited via the internet with four received. Work will be performed in Anniston, Alabama, with an estimated completion date of April 27, 2029. Fiscal 2025 military construction, defense-wide funds in the amount of $51,572,833 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville, Kentucky, is the contracting activity (W912QR-26-C-A028).

Grunley Construction Co. Inc., Rockville, Maryland, was awarded a $45,929,500 firm-fixed-price contract for the new construction of a 57,955 square foot warehouse, an 8,000 linear foot rail siding, and a suspect track for monitoring and inspection of compromised rail cars. Bids were solicited via the internet with three received. Work will be performed in Chambersburg, Pennsylvania, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 17, 2028. Fiscal 2026 military construction, Army funds in the amount of $45,929,500 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Baltimore, Maryland, is the contracting activity (W912DR-26-C-A022).

Bristol Group LLC, Lexington, Kentucky, was awarded a $35,356,272 contract for design-build construction of a small-arms ammunition magazine at Blue Grass Army Depot. Bids were solicited via the internet with four received. Work will be performed in Richmond, Kentucky, with an estimated completion date of June 24, 2029. Fiscal 2025 military construction, Army funds in the amount of $35,356,272 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville, Kentucky, is the contracting activity (W912QR-26-C-A037).

Relyant Global LLC, Maryville, Tennessee, was awarded a $26,133,359 firm-fixed-price contract for construction of an aircraft maintenance hangar. Bids were solicited via the internet with five received. Work will be performed in Comalapa, El Salvador, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 17, 2028. Fiscal 2022 military construction, Navy funds in the amount of $26,133,359 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile, Alabama, is the contracting activity (W51DQV-26-C-A007).

Shipcom Federal Solutions LLC,* Houston, Texas, was awarded a $16,892,413 firm-fixed-price contract for a secure, resilient and recoverable hybrid infrastructure architecture across an active footprint, integrating existing network assets with private 5G, complementary wireless transport and standards-based information technology and operational technology infrastructure. Bids were solicited via the internet with seven received. Work will be performed in Corpus Christi, Texas, with an estimated completion date of Nov. 1, 2027. Fiscal 2026 operation and maintenance, Army funds in the amount of $16,892,413 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, is the contracting activity (W912NW-26-P-A037).

Moran Iron Works Inc.,* Onamay, Michigan, was awarded a $16,429,613 firm-fixed-price contract for miter gate fabrication for the Captain Anthony Meldahl (CAM) Lock and Dam. Bids were solicited via the internet with six received. Work will be performed in Felicity, Ohio with an estimated completion date of Oct. 31, 2029. Fiscal 2026 operation and maintenance, civil funds in the amount of $16,429,613 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Huntington, West Virginia, is the contracting activity (W91237-26-C-A006).

General Dynamics Land Systems, Sterling Heights, Michigan, was awarded a $15,299,831 modification (P00150) to contract (W56HZV-22-C-0012) for Abrams system technical support. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $1,227,184,830. Work will be performed in Sterling Heights, Michigan, with an estimated completion date of Feb. 27, 2031. Fiscal 2026 other procurement, Army funds in the amount of $15,299,831 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Contracting Command, Detroit Arsenal, Michigan, is the contracting activity.

Applied Research Associates Inc., Albuquerque, New Mexico, was awarded a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract for novel munitions and advanced energetics development. The amount of this action is $13,527,395 with a total cumulative face value of $37,744,768. One bid was solicited with one received. Work will be performed in Albuquerque, New Mexico with an estimated completion date of Sept. 17, 2029. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation, Army funds in the amount of $13,527,395 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Contracting Command, Newark, New Jersey, is the contracting activity (W15QKN-26-C-A008).

Curtin Maritime Corp., Long Beach, California was awarded an $11,471,704 firm-fixed-price contract for Wilmington Harbor anchorage and mid-river maintenance dredging. Bids were solicited via the internet with three received. Work will be performed in Wilmington, North Carolina with an estimated completion date of April 30, 2027. Fiscal 2023 civil construction funds; fiscal 2025 civil construction funds; and fiscal 2026 civil construction funds in the amount of $11,471,704 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Wilmington, North Carolina, is the contracting activity (W912PM-26-C-A021).

Skyeton Inc., North Las Vegas, Nevada, was awarded a $10,640,000 firm-fixed-price for Raybird UAS hardware and services. Bids were solicited via the internet with one received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Dec. 15, 2026. U.S. Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, is the contracting activity (W58RGZ-26-F-A026).
